answer: One marble slab per identity, locked by a 70-credit bond. It is fired in an ember kiln, which stamps a key-bound firing mark. Its firing curve enters a public onyx table; the auditor recomputes it and burns the bond on a 5% deviation, reuse, or double filing. Filing k costs 32+5(k-1): 1,000 fakes pay 2,529,500, lock 70,000, vs a 40,000 pool. Rented kilns fail: one key fires five slabs at most. An honest agent files once for 32, keeps its share.
